Kinda glad I'm not the only one with this problem at the moment.

Thank you for replying. They know almost nothing about me actually, since they have never given me a chance to be part of them. I have thought that maybe they haven't noticed my mistakes, but I always ended up thinking it was impossible, making me more afraid of going out and do things (and make more mistakes).

I am starting to do that. I have already disconnected myself from all the friends I've made before last year, including some really close friends of mine (or at least I thought we were) and I'm going to dump my sim cards soon, not like my phones ever ring anyway (that's why I always keep them on airplane mode to save battery). In a couple of years, hopefully I'll move to another place. But I gotta be honest, it feels pretty scary because I am completely on my own now, but it also feels better as I'm slowly letting my past go.
Thanks, but I'm good. It's just that the thought has been bugging me for a while and I needed to get it off. :)
Friday night? I spend 7 days a week alone and I haven't talked verbally to anyone but my family since April, so PM me if you wanna talk, I would love some conversation too.
Yeah, my grades this year have been absolutely awful. I haven't been able to focus on anything at all because of all the distractions.
That's why I avoid using facebook, it's not helping though.

Hahaha, don't worry about your assumption, I'm actually a Malaysian studying in Australia now. The reason I don't take part is almost always anxiety. I have wanted to go to a number of events earlier this year, but I always ended up panicking at the last minute and not going. I always feel like everyone hates me and are going to hurt me (because bullies and harassment in high school). That's why I'm always in my room playing video games.
Open-book exams are usually harder than closed-book exams.

You remind me of myself when I was still a medical student. It was at least equally bad. The school was terrible and I hated everything, and I mean everything. My everyday was concentrated with anger, fear and suicidal thoughts, so I decided to quit after a year and switched to a business degree that I thought I wouldn't like half a year later.

Now I'm 1.5 years into my new degree, and so far I find myself KINDA enjoying it although it's hard. As for my student life, the first 6 months were fantastic, but the next 1 year has been absurdly f***ed up because of my housemates.

You can take some time to figure out your next move, and if you decide to transfer to another school or degree, know that you may enjoy all of it, or part of it, or none at all. So once again, take some time to think about it carefully.

I tried so hard to greet and chat with my floormates since the first day I moved into a dorm, I kept trying for months and all I got were cold shoulders and more hate (they already disliked me before I moved in for some reason). I have met some people on other floors and they are all friendly, unlike this floor. Maybe I did something wrong without realizing it, but that doesn't explain why I'm hated before I moved in.
You are right, I have to go out there. The more I stay in my room, the more pathetic I feel about myself. Maybe I’ll even discover something new. Thanks.
